title: a body reader is buffering or streaming, and only a streaming one consumes the body
scope:
which readers of `Core\Request`'s body may follow which, and why that is a property of the
member rather than a list of pairs. It does not decide `json()`'s signature or its error behaviour,
which are [0097](0097.md) § 8's roster and this goal's own standing decisions.
dependsOnText:
[0097](0097.md) § 8 (the body, the two caps and the streaming reader),
[0105](0105.md) § 2 (a multipart form's non-file parts are buffered into `post()`),
[0095](0095.md) (ambiguous input is refused whole).
validatedBy:
the refusal `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs`'s `claim_body` states to a program,
and the conformance cases that pin a second buffering read answering the same octets.

summary.headline: A request body is read either into a buffer or as a stream, never both
summary.body:
`body`, `post`, `json` and `jsonAs` buffer the request body under the configured size limit and
answer from that buffer, so any of them may follow any other in any order. `bodyStream` and
`files` hand the bytes to the program as they arrive and keep nothing, so each of those may only
be the first thing to read the body. Reading `post()` after walking `files()` still works: the
walk buffers the ordinary fields it passes, and `post()` reads that buffer like any other
buffering reader.
